sheet_from: Data/World34/Tile*.OZJ, from MuMain, decoded under an ai_ prefix: assets/textures is one flat pool, and Lorencia and others already own the bare Tile* names (Crywolf's Object35 shares about sixty of Aida's object sheets too). TileRock05 is a red carpet with an ornate border, a leftover of whatever map Aida was started from, drawn only on the map's edge rows and columns past the walls; at 16:9 it would show as a red strip, so ai_tilerock05.png is a copy of Aida's hay, ai_tileground01.png: ours, marked. A copy and not the same file, because the ground's loader names each surface by its pair of images. TileRock04/06/07 ship and no tile wears them. docs/worlds/aida-port.md.
slot_note: World34 ships TileGrass01.OZT, dark olive blades, which MU grows on slot 0 (terrain.py GRASS_BY_MAP[33]); TileGrass02.OZT is fully transparent, so slot 1 grows nothing. A dark mossy forest of winding clearings over a NoGround ravine (34.5% of the map) that runs from the entrance to the north-east, walled by Object18-20's 13 m rock faces; the safe hall in the north-west (74-93, 5-17).
material_note: Read off the art; the names lie. TileGrass01 is dark moss and clover, the forest floor; TileWood01 is the same painting under another encoding, so grass; TileGrass02 grass and straw over red-brown earth; TileGround01 dry brown hay, and TileGround03 ochre moss with grey lichen (an overlay sheet): grass. TileGround02 is rounded cobbles in dark moss: cobble. TileRock01 grey-green cracked rock: rock. TileRock02 the ruins' mossy brick and TileRock03 pale flagstones in grass: flagstone. TileWater01 the ponds: water.
